title: 1993 AHSME Problem 11
statement: If \(\log_2(\log_2(\log_2(x)))=2,\) then how many digits are in the base-ten representation for \(x?\)

solutions.text: Undoing the logarithms gives \[ \begin{aligned} \log_2(\log_2 x)&=4,\\ \log_2x&=16,\\ x&=2^{16}=65536. \end{aligned} \] This number has \(5\) decimal digits. Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Undo the logarithms one at a time from the outside
The successive values are \(2,\) \(4,\) and \(16\) before solving for \(x\)
